title: Eye Injuries & Chemicals in the Eye
summary: Chemicals in the eye: rinse immediately with lots of clean running water and keep rinsing. Objects in the eye: do not remove anything stuck in it – shield the eye.

callEmergency.headline: Call {EMERGENCY} or get urgent medical help for serious eye injuries
when: Chemical in the eye (keep rinsing while help comes)
Object stuck in the eye, or a cut to the eye
Sudden loss of vision, double vision or severe pain
Blood inside the coloured part of the eye

steps.title: Chemical in the eye
steps.text: Rinse at once with large amounts of clean, lukewarm running water. Hold the eye open and tilt the head so the water runs away from the other eye.
points: Keep rinsing for at least 15–20 minutes, or until help arrives
Remove contact lenses if easy to do

steps.title: Note the chemical
steps.text: Keep the container or label for responders. Use the Hazmat lookup for transport incidents.

steps.title: Object stuck in the eye
steps.text: Do not remove it. Cover the eye with a paper cup or rigid shield that does not press on the object. Ask them to keep both eyes as still as possible.

steps.title: Loose grit or dust
steps.text: Rinse with clean water. Do not rub the eye.

steps.title: Blow to the eye
steps.text: Apply a cold pack wrapped in cloth gently, without pressure on the eye, and get medical advice.

doNot: Do not remove an object stuck in the eye
Do not use anything other than clean water to rinse chemicals

sources.body: American Heart Association and American Red Cross
sources.title: 2024 American Heart Association and American Red Cross Guidelines for First Aid
